s:
Arrange the following laws and policies in chronological order of their enactment or adoption:
A. National Forest Policy, 1952
B. Indian Forest Act, 1927
C. Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
D. Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
x: The correct sequence is the Indian Forest Act, 1927, National Forest Policy, 1952, Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980.
tq: Use the first and last dates to eliminate sequences before checking the middle entries.
sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

s: The first Indian Forest Act was drafted in which year?
x: The first Indian Forest Act was drafted in 1865.
tq: Distinguish the first forest legislation from the later consolidating Act of 1927.
sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following features is associated with the Indian Forest Act, 1878?
o: It established the Animal Welfare Board of India.
It created the Concurrent List for forests and wildlife.
It introduced the 33% forest and tree cover target.
It introduced reserved, protected and village forests.
x: The Indian Forest Act, 1878 introduced the categories of reserved, protected and village forests.
tq: Match the distinctive institutional feature with the correct law and year.
sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

s: The Indian Forest Act, 1927 is best described as a law that
o: consolidated colonial forest legislation and continues to remain in force
created the National Forest Policy after Independence
regulated only wildlife sanctuaries and national parks
transferred forests exclusively to the State List
x: The Indian Forest Act, 1927 was a colonial consolidating law and continues to remain in force.
tq: Select the precise description rather than an option that confuses a forest law with a policy or constitutional provision.
sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act was enacted in 1960.
2. The Animal Welfare Board of India was set up under this Act in 1962.
3. The Act transferred forests and wildlife to the Concurrent List.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Transfer of forests and wildlife to the Concurrent List was associated with the 42nd Amendment in 1976, not the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act.
tq: Find the statement that assigns a constitutional change to the wrong legislation.
sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

s: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment is significant for forest and wildlife governance because it
o: inserted Articles 48A and 51A(g) and placed forests and wildlife in the Concurrent List
created Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act
x: The 42nd Amendment inserted Article 48A, added Article 51A(g), and transferred forests and wildlife to the Concurrent List.
tq: Associate a constitutional amendment with its specific Articles and legislative-list change.
sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Forest Policy, 1988?
o: It brought forests into the Concurrent List.
It set a target of 33% forest and tree cover.
It abolished the Indian Forest Act, 1927.
It created the first three forest categories under Indian law.
x: The National Forest Policy, 1988 set the target of 33% forest and tree cover.
tq: Identify the policy-specific target instead of confusing it with statutory or constitutional changes.
sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

s: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 came into force on
x: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 came into force on 25 October 1980.
tq: Test the exact commencement date rather than merely the enactment year.
sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Environment (Protection) Act — 1986
2. Biological Diversity Act — 2002
3. Forest Rights Act — 2006
4. Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act — 2022
x: All four pairs are correctly matched: the Environment (Protection) Act was enacted in 1986, the Biological Diversity Act in 2002, the Forest Rights Act in 2006, and the Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act in 2022.
tq: Check each year-law pair independently before selecting the comprehensive combination.
sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

s: The Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act, 2023 renamed the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 as the
x: The 2023 amendment renamed it the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980.
tq: Distinguish the exact official title from plausible but unofficial alternatives.
sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

s: The Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 was enforced in
x: Although enacted in 2022, the Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act was enforced in April 2023.
tq: Separate the year of enactment from the year of enforcement.
sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

s: The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 originally contained
x: The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 contained 66 sections in 7 chapters and was subsequently amended in 1991, 2002, 2006 and 2022.
tq: Match the numerical structure of the Act without confusing it with the number of schedules.
sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following statements regarding the definitions in the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 is correct?
o: Wildlife is defined in Section 26 and animal in Section 35.
Section 2(1) defines wildlife, while Section 2(37) defines animal.
Section 2(37) defines wildlife, while Section 2(1) defines animal.
Both wildlife and animal are defined in Section 62.
x: Section 2(37) defines wildlife and Section 2(1) defines animal.
tq: Discriminate between closely placed section numbers and their assigned definitions.
sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

s: Under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, the term “animal” includes
o: only mammals and birds found in forests
only domesticated animals and their young
plants, fungi and microorganisms occurring in wildlife habitats
amphibians, birds, mammals, reptiles, their young, and the eggs of birds and reptiles
x: The statutory definition includes amphibians, birds, mammals, reptiles and their young, along with the eggs of birds and reptiles.
tq: Choose the complete statutory definition rather than a narrower everyday meaning.
sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to the schedules of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 after the 2022 amendment, consider the following statements:
1. Schedule I provides the highest protection.
2. Schedule II provides lesser protection.
3. Schedule III contains protected plants.
4. Schedule IV contains specimens listed in the CITES Appendices.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements are correct for the four-schedule framework after the 2022 amendment.
tq: Use the post-amendment schedule structure as a complete classification question.
sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly compares the schedules before and after the 2022 amendment to the Wild Life (Protection) Act?
o: The number of schedules was increased from four to six.
The separate vermin schedule was retained as Schedule IV.
Protected plants were shifted from Schedule VI to Schedule I without any new schedule structure.
The number of schedules was reduced from six to four.
x: The 2022 amendment reduced the schedules from six to four and deleted the separate vermin schedule.
tq: Compare the old and new frameworks by focusing first on the numerical change.
sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following species-category pairs is correctly matched under the post-2022 schedule framework?
o: Indian flying fox — Schedule IV as a CITES specimen
Dugong — Schedule II with lesser protection
Blackbuck — Schedule III as a protected plant
x: The Indian flying fox was formerly listed as vermin in Schedule V but is placed in Schedule II after the 2022 framework. Blackbuck and dugong are included in Schedule I.
tq: Track the change in status of a familiar species instead of applying the old vermin classification.
sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Schedule IV of the Wild Life (Protection) Act after the 2022 amendment:
1. It contains specimens listed in the CITES Appendices.
2. It is the schedule for protected plants.
3. It is the schedule for invasive alien species.
Which of the statements given above is correct?
x: Schedule IV contains CITES-listed specimens. Protected plants are in Schedule III, while invasive alien species are regulated through a separate power of the Centre.
tq: Reject options that swap neighbouring schedule subjects and statutory powers.
sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

s: After deletion of the separate vermin schedule, which authority may declare a wild animal not included in Schedule I as vermin?
o: The National Board for Wildlife through a judicial order
The local authority without any restriction on area or period
The Central Government by notification under Section 62
The State Legislature by amendment of Schedule I
x: Under Section 62, the Central Government may declare a wild animal not in Schedule I as vermin for a specified area and period by notification.
tq: Ask who would perform the statutory power and check its area-and-period limits.
sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of inclusion of an animal in Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act?
o: The species may be hunted freely without restriction during the notified period.
Hunting and trade are generally prohibited except in special cases allowed by the Act.
The species receives the highest statutory protection.
x: Schedule I species receive the highest protection; hunting and trade are prohibited except in special cases permitted by the Act. Free hunting is not allowed.
tq: Find the option that reverses the legal effect of the highest-protection category.
sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act?
1. Mugger crocodile — Schedule I
2. Rock eagle-owl — Schedule I
3. Common crow — Schedule I
4. Blackbuck — Schedule I
x: The mugger crocodile, rock eagle-owl and blackbuck are in Schedule I. The common crow was included in the former vermin Schedule V, not Schedule I.
tq: Separate high-protection species from a former vermin species.
sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

s: A specified plant included in the protected-plant schedule cannot ordinarily be
o: cultivated in every circumstance without regulatory permission
observed or photographed in its natural habitat
picked, uprooted or traded without permission
x: A specified plant cannot be picked, uprooted or traded without permission. The law regulates these activities rather than prohibiting observation or scientific description.
tq: Apply the statutory restriction to the conduct described in the scenario.
sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

s: Under the Indian Forest Act, 1927, which forest category receives the most stringent protection?
x: Reserved forests receive the most stringent protection; felling, grazing and hunting are barred unless expressly permitted, and the State controls management.
tq: Identify the category associated with the strictest restrictions and State control.
sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

s: A reserved forest is assigned to a village community under which category of the Indian Forest Act, 1927?
x: A village forest is a reserved forest assigned to a village community.
tq: Use the statutory relationship between a reserved forest and the village-community category.
sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

s: Which statement correctly describes a protected forest under the Indian Forest Act, 1927?
o: It can be managed only by the Central Government.
All felling, grazing and hunting are automatically barred.
Activities are allowed unless specifically prohibited.
It is a reserved forest assigned to a village community.
x: In a protected forest, activities are allowed unless specifically prohibited. The relevant provisions are in Chapter IV, Sections 29–34.
tq: Distinguish the default rule for protected forests from the stricter rule for reserved forests.
sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

s: Which pair correctly indicates the statutory provisions relating to reserved forests and village forests under the Indian Forest Act, 1927?
o: Reserved forests — Sections 3–27; village forests — Section 28
Reserved forests — Sections 29–34; village forests — Section 35
Reserved forests — Section 26 only; village forests — Sections 3–27
Reserved forests — Section 62; village forests — Sections 29–34
x: Reserved forests are covered in Chapter II, Sections 3–27, while village forests are covered in Chapter III, Section 28.
tq: Start from the sure section range and reject options that shift categories between chapters.
sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

s: Section 26 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927 primarily deals with
o: regulation of forests that are not government property
assignment of reserved forests to village communities
acts prohibited in a reserved forest, including punishable trespass
removal of bamboo from non-forest land without a permit
x: Section 26 lists prohibited acts in a reserved forest and makes trespass punishable.
tq: Match the offence section with its specific prohibited conduct.
sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

s: Section 35 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927 empowers the State to regulate
o: only reserved forests owned by the Union Government
forests that are not government property
wild animals declared vermin under Section 62 of the Wildlife Act
x: Section 35 permits the State to regulate forests that are not government property.
tq: Identify the correct authority and subject of the statutory power.
sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

s: The 2017 amendment to the Indian Forest Act, enacted as an Act in 2018, removed which item grown outside forest areas from the definition of “tree” under Section 2(7)?
x: The amendment removed bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of tree under Section 2(7).
tq: Identify the exact plant involved in the amendment rather than a commercially important tree chosen as a distractor.
sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

s: What was the practical effect of removing bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of “tree” under the 2017 amendment?
o: Bamboo was brought under Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act.
All bamboo cultivation was prohibited on private land.
Bamboo on private or non-forest land could be felled and transported without a permit.
Bamboo could be felled only in reserved forests without a permit.
x: Bamboo grown on private or non-forest land could thereafter be felled and transported without a permit.
tq: Translate a definitional amendment into its practical legal consequence.
sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

s: Which criticism of the Indian Forest Act, 1927 encouraged later reforms towards community rights?
o: It gave unrestricted ownership of forests to forest-dwellers.
It dealt exclusively with marine biodiversity.
It was viewed as harming the livelihoods of forest-dwellers.
It abolished all State control over forest management.
x: The Act has been criticised for harming forest-dwellers’ livelihoods, contributing to reform efforts focused on community rights.
tq: Link the criticism to the reform direction without confusing it with the Act’s formal forest categories.
sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

s: Under the National Forest Policy, 1952, which one of the following combinations correctly represents the prescribed forest-cover targets?
o: Two-thirds of the land under forest, including 60% in hills and 25% in plains
One-fourth of the land under forest, including 50% in hills and 33% in plains
One-third of the land under forest, including 25% in hills and 60% in plains
One-third of the land under forest, including 60% in hills and 25% in plains
x: The 1952 policy aimed at one-third of the total land under forest, with 60% forest cover in hills and 25% in plains.
tq: Split the overall target from the separate hill and plain targets.
sec: National Forest Policy 1952 and 1988 - objectives and forest-cover target  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to the National Forest Policy, 1988, consider the following statements:
1. It envisages forest or tree cover over 33% of the geographical area.
2. It prescribes two-thirds forest or tree cover for hilly and mountainous regions.
3. It requires at least two-thirds of the entire country's land to be under forest.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The two-thirds target applies to hilly and mountainous regions, not to the entire country; hence statement 3 is false.
tq: Find the scope of the two-thirds figure before selecting the coded option.
sec: National Forest Policy 1952 and 1988 - objectives and forest-cover target  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is NOT an objective associated with the National Forest Policy, 1988?
o: Promoting a massive people's movement involving women
Replacing all natural forests with commercial plantations
Checking soil erosion and desert spread
Meeting the fuelwood, fodder and minor forest produce needs of rural and tribal people
x: The policy supports ecological stability, conservation, afforestation, social forestry and local needs. It does not seek to replace all natural forests with commercial plantations.
tq: Identify the option that reverses the conservation-oriented objective.
sec: National Forest Policy 1952 and 1988 - objectives and forest-cover target  [APPSC]

s:
The National Forest Policy, 1988, supports which combination of measures?
1. Corridors between protected areas
2. Fuel-efficient chulhas
3. Massive afforestation and social forestry
4. Promotion of desert spread
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The policy supports protected-area corridors, fuel-efficient chulhas, afforestation and social forestry. Promotion of desert spread is contrary to its objectives.
tq: Reject the statement that contradicts the policy's ecological purpose.
sec: National Forest Policy 1952 and 1988 - objectives and forest-cover target  [APPSC]

s: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is best described as an umbrella law dealing with
o: only the diversion of forest land
access and benefit sharing from biological resources
only the declaration of tiger reserves
x: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is an umbrella law for environmental protection and pollution control.
tq: Distinguish the umbrella environmental law from sector-specific statutes.
sec: Acts protecting wild animals, birds and plants - WPA vs EPA vs FCA, AWBI  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 — Regulation of diversion of forest land
2. Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 — Parent Act of the Animal Welfare Board of India
3. Biological Diversity Act, 2002 — Access and benefit sharing
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: All three pairs are correctly matched. The Forest (Conservation) Act checks deforestation and regulates diversion, the PCA Act led to the AWBI, and the Biological Diversity Act implements access and benefit sharing.
tq: Verify each Act against its distinctive subject before using the combination code.
sec: Acts protecting wild animals, birds and plants - WPA vs EPA vs FCA, AWBI  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the National Green Tribunal's jurisdiction as described in the legal framework?
o: It hears cases under the Forest Rights Act but not under the Forest (Conservation) Act.
It has jurisdiction only over the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act.
It hears cases under the Wildlife (Protection) Act but not under the Environment (Protection) Act.
It hears cases under seven laws, including the Forest (Conservation) Act, Environment (Protection) Act and Biological Diversity Act.
x: The NGT hears cases under seven specified laws, including the FCA 1980, EPA 1986 and BD Act 2002. The framework states that it cannot hear cases under the WPA 1972 or FRA 2006.
tq: Use the inclusion and exclusion of statutes to separate NGT jurisdiction from ordinary wildlife law.
sec: Acts protecting wild animals, birds and plants - WPA vs EPA vs FCA, AWBI  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT the name of an Act in the environmental legal framework described here?
x: There is no Act called the Nature (Protection) Act, 2000. The other three are recognised environmental statutes.
tq: Spot the look-alike title rather than accepting a familiar-sounding statute.
sec: Acts protecting wild animals, birds and plants - WPA vs EPA vs FCA, AWBI  [APPSC]

s: The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau was constituted in 2007 under the administrative control of
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
x: The Bureau was constituted in 2007 under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
tq: Apply the 'who established or administers the body?' method.
sec: Wildlife Crime Control Bureau - HQ, regional offices, operations  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following correctly lists the five regional offices of the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau?
o: Delhi, Jaipur, Hyderabad, Guwahati and Kochi
Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai and Jabalpur
New Delhi, Bhopal, Bengaluru, Patna and Srinagar
Kolkata, Lucknow, Pune, Ranchi and Visakhapatnam
x: The five regional offices are at Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai and Jabalpur.
tq: Check the complete membership of the fixed regional-office list.
sec: Wildlife Crime Control Bureau - HQ, regional offices, operations  [APPSC]

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Operation)
A. Save Kurma
B. Softgold
C. Clean Art
D. Thunderbird

List-II (Focus)
1. Turtles
2. Shahtoosh
3. Mongoose-hair brushes
4. INTERPOL-led operation

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Save Kurma concerns turtles, Softgold concerns shahtoosh, Clean Art targets mongoose-hair brushes, and Thunderbird is INTERPOL-led.
tq: Start from the sure operation–subject pair and eliminate codes.
sec: Wildlife Crime Control Bureau - HQ, regional offices, operations  [APPSC]

s: The WCCB operation known as 'Birbil' is associated with illegal activities involving
x: Operation Birbil deals with wildlife crime involving wild cats and birds.
tq: Discriminate between similarly named wildlife-crime operations by their target species.
sec: Wildlife Crime Control Bureau - HQ, regional offices, operations  [APPSC]

s:
Under the original Section 2 of the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, prior approval of the Central Government was required for which of the following?
1. De-reservation of a forest
2. Use of forest land for a non-forest purpose
3. Clearing of trees on forest land
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The original Section 2 required prior Central approval for de-reservation, non-forest use of forest land and clearing of trees.
tq: Treat each listed trigger for Central approval as a separate statutory condition.
sec: Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 - diversion approval, 2023 amendment, AP data  [APPSC]

s: The renamed Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 came into effect on
x: The 2023 amendment came into force with effect from 29 December 2023.
tq: Separate the commencement date from the dates defining covered or excluded land.
sec: Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 - diversion approval, 2023 amendment, AP data  [APPSC]

s:
After the 2023 amendment, which categories of land are covered by the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980?
1. Land notified as forest under the Indian Forest Act, 1927 or another law
2. Land recorded as forest in government records on or after 25 October 1980
3. Every private agricultural field having one or more trees
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The amended Act covers land notified as forest under the IFA or another law and land recorded as forest in government records on or after 25 October 1980. It does not cover every private agricultural field with trees.
tq: Test the statutory definition by separating included categories from an overbroad claim.
sec: Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 - diversion approval, 2023 amendment, AP data  [APPSC]

s: Which land is excluded from the coverage of the amended forest-conservation law?
o: Forest land proposed for a non-forest purpose after the amendment
Land converted to non-forest use before 12 December 1996
Land recorded as forest in government records after 25 October 1980
Land notified as forest under the Indian Forest Act, 1927
x: Land converted to non-forest use before 12 December 1996 is excluded from the amended law's coverage.
tq: Look for the date-based exception to the general coverage rule.
sec: Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 - diversion approval, 2023 amendment, AP data  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is NOT listed as an exemption from the requirement of Central approval under the amended forest-conservation framework?
o: Zoos and safaris under the Wildlife (Protection) Act
All commercial mining projects beyond 100 km of an international boundary
Strategic linear projects within 100 km of the International Border, LoC or LAC
x: The listed exemptions include specified strategic linear projects, eco-tourism facilities, zoos and safaris under the WPA, and minor infrastructure. A blanket exemption for all commercial mining projects is not provided.
tq: Reject the broad commercial exemption that is not among the specified categories.
sec: Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 - diversion approval, 2023 amendment, AP data  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to compensatory afforestation under the forest-conservation framework, consider the following statements:
1. It requires non-forest land of equal area where such land is available.
2. If equal non-forest land is unavailable, twice the area of degraded forest land is used.
3. Net Present Value is paid in addition to compensatory afforestation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Equal-area non-forest land is preferred; otherwise twice the degraded forest area is used, along with payment of NPV.
tq: Check whether the alternatives are cumulative rather than mutually exclusive.
sec: Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 - diversion approval, 2023 amendment, AP data  [APPSC]

s: Under the Van (S.E.S.) Amendment Rules, 2025, which activities on leased forest land are treated as forestry activities?
o: Only tourism infrastructure and road widening
x: The 2025 rules treat assisted natural regeneration and plantation on leased forest land as forestry activities. Compensatory afforestation and NPV do not apply to these activities.
tq: Identify the exact paired activities and avoid substituting unrelated land uses.
sec: Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 - diversion approval, 2023 amendment, AP data  [APPSC]

s: For Andhra Pradesh, the cumulative forest area diverted under the forest-conservation law up to 2017–18 was
x: The cumulative diversion figure for Andhra Pradesh up to 2017–18 was 26,924.34 hectares.
tq: Match the precise figure with its corresponding reporting period.
sec: Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 - diversion approval, 2023 amendment, AP data  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following Andhra Pradesh forest-diversion figures in chronological order of the reporting period:
A. 27,641.252 hectares up to 31 December 2024
B. 26,924.34 hectares up to 2017–18
C. 149.5687 hectares diverted between 1 April and 31 December 2025
D. 27,303.18 hectares up to 2021–22
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The sequence is 2017–18, 2021–22, 31 December 2024 and the period from 1 April to 31 December 2025: B, D, A, C.
tq: Arrange the figures by their reporting dates, not by their numerical size.
sec: Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 - diversion approval, 2023 amendment, AP data  [APPSC]

s: The cumulative forest area diverted in Andhra Pradesh under the relevant forest-conservation law up to 31 December 2024 was
x: The cumulative diversion figure reported for Andhra Pradesh up to 31 December 2024 was 27,641.252 hectares.
tq: Use the date attached to the cumulative figure to avoid confusing it with an earlier total or a later increment.
sec: Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 - diversion approval, 2023 amendment, AP data  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the 2002 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act?
o: Conservation Reserve — government-owned buffer or corridor
Community Reserve — exclusively Central Government land
Conservation Reserve — private land managed by a Community Reserve Management Committee
Community Reserve — statutory body for tiger conservation
x: Conservation Reserves are government-owned buffers or corridors. Community Reserves concern private or community land and are managed by a Community Reserve Management Committee.
tq: Separate the ownership basis of Conservation Reserves from that of Community Reserves.
sec: WPA amendments 2002 and 2006 - bodies and categories added

s: The 2002 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife with the
x: The 2002 amendment replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife with the National Board for Wildlife.
tq: Track the institutional replacement rather than confusing it with bodies created in 2006.
sec: WPA amendments 2002 and 2006 - bodies and categories added

s: The 2022 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act is associated with
o: introduction of the Tiger Conservation Plan requirement under Section 38V(3)
replacement of the Indian Board for Wildlife by the National Board for Wildlife
creation of the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau
rationalisation of schedules and addition of invasive alien species
x: The 2022 amendment rationalised the schedules and added invasive alien species. The other options relate to the 2002 or 2006 amendments.
tq: Use the amendment timeline to separate later schedule changes from earlier institutional reforms.
sec: WPA amendments 2002 and 2006 - bodies and categories added

s:
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 transferred which of the following subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List?
1. Forests
2. Protection of wild animals and birds
3. Public health
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The 42nd Amendment transferred forests through Entry 17A and protection of wild animals and birds through Entry 17B to the Concurrent List. Public health was not transferred by this amendment.
tq: Identify the two related entries and reject the unrelated subject.
sec: Related provisions - list placement, Godavarman, NBWL chair

s: Which one of the following provisions was inserted into the Directive Principles of State Policy by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
x: Article 48A, directing the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife, was inserted by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
tq: Use the constitutional-part distinction to separate a DPSP from a Fundamental Duty.
sec: Related provisions - list placement, Godavarman, NBWL chair

s: Article 51A(g), relating to protection of the natural environment, belongs to which part of the Constitution?
x: Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty requiring citizens to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife.
tq: Discriminate between the similarly related Articles 48A and 51A(g).
sec: Related provisions - list placement, Godavarman, NBWL chair

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad case:
1. The expression ‘forest’ covers every area recorded as forest in government records.
2. The definition applies irrespective of ownership.
3. The interpretation is confined only to notified national parks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Godavarman interpretation covers every area recorded as forest in government records, regardless of ownership. It is not confined to national parks.
tq: Find the incorrect limiting statement.
sec: Related provisions - list placement, Godavarman, NBWL chair

s: Who chairs the National Board for Wildlife?
x: The National Board for Wildlife is chaired by the Prime Minister. Its Standing Committee is chaired by the Union Environment Minister.
tq: Apply the ‘who chairs this body?’ authority trap.
sec: Related provisions - list placement, Godavarman, NBWL chair

s: The Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife is chaired by the:
o: Chief Minister of the concerned State
